sentences.en:
We wonder at Caliph ‘Umar's
claim that, since we have the Qur'an in our midst, we do not stand in need of any guide.

It is just like a
man saying that, since we have books of medicine, we do not require a physician.

Obviously it is a false
assertion because a man who cannot solve his problems by reading the books of medicine must consult
a physician.
The same thing holds true in the case of the Holy Qur'an.

Everyone cannot derive advantage from it
through his ability.
He must necessarily turn to those who have knowledge of the Holy Qur'an."

The Holy Qur'an says:
"And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those among
them who can search out the knowledge of it would have known it."

(4:83)
In fact the real book is the heart of one who possesses knowledge, as the Holy Qur'an says:
"Nay these are clear communications in the breasts of those who are granted knowledge."

(29:49)
Accordingly, ‘Ali said: "I am the speaking Book of Allah, and this Qur'an is the mute book."
So according to the people of knowledge ‘Umar was mistaken.

It was a great injustice to the Holy
Prophet of Allah that he was prevented from writing his will.

Abu bakr was not prevented from writing his will
With regard to your repeated claim that Abu Bakr and ‘Umar were not prevented from writing their wills, I
admit it is true.

It is surprising, as all your historians and traditionists have recorded in their authentic
books that Caliph Abu Bakr, at the time of his death, asked Uthman Ibn Affan to write down what he
(Abu Bakr) was saying.
He wrote down whatever Abu Bakr dictated to him.
